quick.summary: Stop arguments over past technical choices by writing down the trade-offs you made.
quick.takeaway: Always log the context, options, choice, and consequences of a big decision.

parts.title: Logging architecture choices

beats.line: We picked a new database last year. Why does nobody remember the reason?
Like finding a strange road sign in your town and having no idea why.
Yes. Now the new engineers want to tear it down and start over.
Because they only see the cost today, not the problem it solved yesterday.
Every choice has a cost. You traded cheap storage for faster search.
But how do we prove that to the new team?
You need an architecture decision record.
Can I just say a choice log?
A choice log is perfect.
So what exactly goes into this log to stop the arguments?

parts.cliff: The four things every choice log needs.

beats.line: You need four simple things to make the log work.
What is the first thing?
The context. What problem were you trying to solve?
We needed faster search for millions of records.
Second is the options considered. Third is the choice you made.
And the fourth thing?
The consequences. What gets better, and what gets worse?
Search is faster, but our bill goes up every month.
Exactly. To change it later, they must read the log first.
They understand the trade before complaining about the bill.
That prevents repeating old mistakes.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of a choice log?
options: To explain why a past technical decision was made.
To track bugs in the software code.
To list the daily tasks of the engineering team.
To monitor the speed of the current database.
quiz.explanation: A log preserves the context of your choices, so future teams understand the trade-offs you faced.

quiz.question: A good choice log only lists the positive outcomes of a decision.
quiz.explanation: You must record the consequences, including the downsides. Every architectural choice has a cost.
